reporting-org.narrative: Siasa Place (SP) is a civic-tech youth-led non-governmental organization (NGO), established in 2015 that specializes in working with grassroots youth, in building institutional structures to support youth participation in politics and good governance. SP targets youth (men and women aged 18 to 35 years) and develops their skills in policy review, supporting the creation of youth-friendly platforms for public participation in decision-making processes, including the budget process and social accountability. SP works in 12 counties including Uasin Gishu, Kakamega, Busia, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Migori, Kericho, Nakuru, Nairobi, Kitui, Lamu, and Mombasa.

title.narrative: Strengthening the Power of Youth Voices quarterly report October 2022 - December 2022

description.narrative: During the first quarter of the program (October to December 2022), several key activities were implemented. The partners held a Program Implementation Strategy Meeting to agree on the implementation approach and developed a work plan for the quarter. Baseline activities commenced, including the conduction of inception meetings in Kericho and Busia counties, two of the six targeted counties. These meetings helped establish foundational partnerships with local duty bearers and facilitated early engagement with county governments. However, the program faced challenges due to the slow transition within county governments following recent elections. Many counties had newly elected governors, and in some cases, even returning governors awaited confirmation amidst potential administrative reshuffles. This situation delayed full engagement, with only two counties allowing inception meetings and designating officers to work with the program, while the other four had to reschedule activities pending government reorganization. The delays also impacted the baseline survey, as county government participation was critical. The program also faced hurdles with slow uptake of technology, which affected data collection during the baseline, and hesitance from some new counties to fully engage with the project. Moving forward, the program plans to train and support the youth leaders identified to spearhead advocacy efforts around key issues, fast-track the finalization of MOUs with the counties, and pursue partnerships aimed at the economic empowerment of youth. The program will focus on completing the program activities that had been rescheduled in the next quarter
